neighbours.label: ' at' or ' in' opening a partial-occurrence qualifier after an evaluative predicate ('clumsy at times', 'dense in places'): the judgement holds only some of the time or in some parts; locative and clock-time 'at'/'in' stay low
fire: The lecture was boring at times, though the ending was clever.
His acting is wooden in places, but the dialogue is sharp.
The trail gets steep and slippery in places after heavy rain.
Critics found the novel confusing at times and slow elsewhere.
The children can be loud at times, but they mean well.
The paint looked patchy in places on the north wall.
My manager is demanding at times, yet always fair.
The documentary is painful at times to watch, but it matters.
quiet: The lecture was held at the town hall on Tuesday evening.
His acting school is in Chicago, near the lake.
The trail starts at the car park behind the church.
Critics gathered at the festival to see the premiere.
The children are at school until three o'clock.
The paint is stored in the shed behind the garage.
My manager is in a meeting until noon today.
The documentary premieres in March on public television.
